issues.description: Default flip from EXTERNAL to FIXED silently changes turn semantics for existing users
issues.detail: The default `turn_detection_mode` was EXTERNAL and is now FIXED. That is a change in the time-and-identity contract of who finalizes a turn: previously the framework's external endpointer drove it; now the plugin does. Existing callers who relied on the default get different behavior with no migration note in the docstring. State the change in semantics, not just the new enum value.

issues.description: `_enable_vad` complects two distinct concepts under one boolean
issues.detail: `_enable_vad` is now defined as 'mode is not FIXED and not EXTERNAL'. That single name is doing two jobs: 'does the plugin emit VAD frames' and 'does the plugin own endpointing.' These can drift. A small data-driven predicate or two named flags (`emits_vad_frames`, `owns_endpointing`) would decompose the concern and make the matrix of modes explicit rather than implicit in a negation.

issues.description: Frame-type switch from UserStoppedSpeakingFrame to VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame is a value-meaning change without an explanation
issues.detail: The finalization trigger moved from `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` to `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame`. Those are different facts about the world: one is 'the user stopped' (whoever decided), the other is 'VAD detected stop.' If the plugin is in FIXED mode and VAD is disabled upstream, this branch may never fire. The reasoning should be written down where the dispatch happens, not only in the changelog.

issues.description: `speech_segment_config` is always overwritten even when `split_sentences` is None
issues.detail: `config.speech_segment_config = SpeechSegmentConfig(emit_sentences=params.split_sentences or False)` runs unconditionally. If a user never set `split_sentences`, the code still constructs a config object and forces `emit_sentences=False`, clobbering whatever default the SDK version provides. The simple form is: only assign when the user explicitly opted in. Let the SDK keep its own default otherwise.

issues.description: Commented-out `start_processing_metrics` call moved but not resolved
issues.detail: The line `# await self.start_processing_metrics()` was relocated from after the broadcast/interruption pair to before it. Dead commented code with no explanation is incidental noise; either it belongs (uncomment with reasoning) or it does not (delete). Moving it changes nothing at runtime and leaves a reader wondering about intent.

issues.description: `split_sentences` docstring describes behavior but not its interaction with turn modes
issues.detail: The new `split_sentences` parameter is documented as 'emit finalized sentences mid-turn,' but the docstring does not say how this composes with `turn_detection_mode` or with `include_partials`. These are three knobs that all shape the value-stream of transcripts over time. A reader cannot tell from the spec what combinations are meaningful without reading the SDK.

review.summary: The diff is a small, targeted update to track an SDK version bump, and most of it is plumbing. The substantive concerns are about meaning, not mechanism: the default `turn_detection_mode` flips from EXTERNAL to FIXED, which silently moves the identity of "who owns end-of-turn" from the framework to the plugin; `_enable_vad` now complects two distinct questions under one negated predicate; and the finalization trigger changes from `UserStoppedSpeakingFrame` to `VADUserStoppedSpeakingFrame`, which is a different fact about the world. None of these is hard to fix — they are easy. They are just not yet simple.
